'''David Francis Barrow''' (November 14, 1888 – February 4, 1970) was an American mathematician who introduced [[Barrow's inequality]] in 1937.

Barrow's father, [[David Crenshaw Barrow Jr.]], was also a mathematician, and served as chancellor of the [[University of Georgia]] from 1906 to 1925. His son, David F. Barrow, did his undergraduate studies at the University of Georgia and then studied at [[Harvard University]], where he earned his [[Doctor of Philosophy|PhD]] in 1913. After a year abroad, he taught for two years at the [[University of Texas]], and then at the [[Sheffield Scientific School]]. After a brief stint in the U.S. armed services, he joined the faculty of his father's university in 1920. He became a full professor in 1923, and chaired the mathematics department in 1944–1945.<ref>[https://www.math.uga.edu/history-mathematics-uga The History of Mathematics at the  University of Georgia, Department of Mathematics, the University of Georgia] {{webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20080209161759/http://www.math.uga.edu/about_us/history.html |date=2008-02-09 }}.</ref>
